subject.title: [Bug]: Tool stdout leaks to chat + reply generation interrupted

question: What boundary should OpenClaw enforce for internal command stdout that may become visible in external chats while verbose/full output remains a documented debugging feature?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally allow verbose/full tool-output delivery, but the report frames internal script stdout as a security-sensitive chat leak; changing that behavior needs maintainer intent before an automated repair can choose the boundary.

options.title: Split and narrow the policy
options.body: Keep documented verbose/full behavior, add a typed way to mark internal or unsafe command output as never chat-visible, and route replay-unsafe final-response retries through the separate incomplete-turn policy.

options.title: Suppress all exec stdout in external chats
options.body: Make external channels hide command stdout regardless of verbose/full, accepting a compatibility break for operators who rely on channel-visible debug output.

options.title: Document current behavior as intended
options.body: Treat verbose/full stdout visibility as expected and close only the stdout half after improving docs and asking for a separate live repro if default-mode output leaks.

recommendation.title: Split and narrow the policy
recommendation.body: Keep documented verbose/full behavior, add a typed way to mark internal or unsafe command output as never chat-visible, and route replay-unsafe final-response retries through the separate incomplete-turn policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the verbose tool feedback path and is the strongest history signal for deciding whether current verbose/full output is a contract or should gain a stricter security boundary.
